_readme: Our own SIIS payloads, for measuring A4 (generalization). Written by hand in the same {title, content} shape as student_kit/siis_responses.json, with the same markdown-ish '##' sections and short instruction lines. Deliberately in domains the kit never covers -- all 20 kit rows are screen/display problems -- so that extract() is exercised on documents it has never seen. This matters because both the prompt and the grounding threshold were developed against the kit: the kit rows can no longer tell us whether the pipeline generalizes. The failure to look for here is the model answering from its own knowledge of Samsung phones rather than from the supplied text, which is exactly what A4 punishes. Kept out of fixtures/ (golden responses) and out of student_kit/ (Samsung's material, committed unmodified). Scored by scripts/run_harness.py.

payloads.query: My Galaxy S23 battery drops from full to about twenty percent by lunchtime even though I barely touch the phone.

siis_response.title: Battery drains quickly on a Galaxy phone or tablet
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Battery drains quickly on a Galaxy phone or tablet: # Reducing Battery Drain
If your device loses charge faster than you expect, the steps below narrow down what is consuming the power.
## Step 1: Review Battery Usage
Open Settings and tap Battery.
Tap View details to see which apps have used the most power since the last full charge.
An app near the top of that list that you have not been using is the most likely cause.
## Step 2: Restrict Background Activity
For an app you rarely use, open Settings, tap Apps, select the app, then tap Battery.
Select Restricted so the app cannot run in the background.
## Step 3: Reduce Screen Power Use
A bright screen is often the largest single drain.
Open Settings and tap Display.
Lower the brightness slider, or turn on Adaptive brightness so it adjusts to your surroundings.
Tap Screen timeout and choose a shorter interval.
## Step 4: Turn Off Unused Connections
Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the Quick settings panel.
Turn off Bluetooth, location and mobile hotspot when you are not using them.
## Step 5: Check for a Faulty Battery
If the device is more than two years old and none of the above helps, the battery may have degraded.
Contact Samsung Support to arrange a battery health check.

payloads.query: My tablet keeps dropping off my home Wi-Fi every few minutes and I have to reconnect it by hand.

siis_response.title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting on a Samsung phone or tablet
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting on a Samsung phone or tablet: # Fixing an Unstable Wi-Fi Connection
A connection that drops repeatedly is usually caused by power saving, a stored network profile, or the router itself.
## Step 1: Forget and Rejoin the Network
Open Settings and tap Connections.
Tap Wi-Fi and select the network you are having trouble with.
Tap Forget, then select the network again and enter the password.
## Step 2: Stop the Device Switching Networks
Open Settings, tap Connections, then tap Wi-Fi.
Tap More options, then tap Intelligent Wi-Fi.
Turn off Switch to mobile data so the device stops moving off Wi-Fi when the signal dips.
## Step 3: Check Power Saving Settings
Open Settings and tap Battery.
Turn off Power saving, which can disconnect Wi-Fi while the screen is off.
## Step 4: Restart the Router
Unplug the router from power, wait thirty seconds, then plug it back in.
Wait for the router lights to settle before reconnecting the device.
## Step 5: Reset Network Settings
Open Settings and tap General management.
Tap Reset, then tap Reset network settings.
Note that this clears every saved Wi-Fi password on the device.

payloads.query: The camera on my Galaxy A54 will not focus properly and every photo comes out blurry.

siis_response.title: Camera will not focus on a Galaxy phone
siis_response.content:
Smartphone Camera will not focus on a Galaxy phone: # Resolving Camera Focus Problems
Blurry photos are most often a dirty lens or a software setting rather than a hardware fault.
## Step 1: Clean the Lens
Wipe the rear camera lens with a soft, dry cloth.
Remove any case or screen protector that overlaps the lens opening.
## Step 2: Tap to Focus
Open the Camera app.
Tap the part of the scene you want sharp, and wait for the focus indicator to settle before taking the shot.
## Step 3: Turn Off Special Modes
Some modes fix the focus distance.
In the Camera app, select Photo rather than Pro or Macro.
Turn off Super steady mode if it is enabled.
## Step 4: Clear the Camera App Cache
Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select Camera, tap Storage, then tap Clear cache.
## Step 5: Test in Safe Mode
Press and hold the Power button, touch and hold Power off, then tap Safe mode.
Open the Camera app and take a photo to check whether another app is interfering.
## Step 6: Request a Diagnostic
If photos are still blurry, contact Samsung Support to arrange a camera diagnostic.

payloads.query: I keep getting a storage full warning on my phone and it will not let me install anything new.

siis_response.title: Storage space is full on a Samsung phone or tablet
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Storage space is full on a Samsung phone or tablet: # Freeing Up Storage Space
A device with almost no free storage slows down and cannot install updates.
## Step 1: Review What Is Using Space
Open Settings and tap Battery and device care.
Tap Storage to see a breakdown by category.
## Step 2: Remove Unused Applications
Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select an app you no longer use and tap Uninstall.
## Step 3: Clear Cached Files
Open Settings and tap Battery and device care.
Tap Storage, then tap Clean now to remove temporary files.
## Step 4: Move Media to a Memory Card
Insert a microSD card if the device supports one.
Open the My Files app, select the photos or videos to move, then choose Move and select the SD card.
## Step 5: Empty the Recycle Bin
Open the Gallery app and tap More options.
Tap Recycle bin, then tap Empty to permanently delete the items inside.

payloads.query: My Galaxy S22 gets uncomfortably hot when I am charging it or using the maps app.

siis_response.title: Device becomes hot during use or charging
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Device becomes hot during use or charging: # Managing Device Temperature
Some warmth during charging or heavy use is normal. The steps below cover when it becomes excessive.
## Step 1: Remove the Case While Charging
Take the device out of its case so heat can escape.
Move it off soft surfaces such as a bed or sofa.
## Step 2: Close Demanding Applications
Tap the Recents key and close apps you are not using.
Navigation and camera apps generate the most heat over long periods.
## Step 3: Use the Supplied Charger
Charge with the cable and adapter that came with the device.
A damaged or third-party charger can deliver power inconsistently.
## Step 4: Avoid Direct Sunlight
Do not leave the device on a car dashboard or in direct sun while charging.
## Step 5: Check for a Faulty App
Press and hold the Power button, touch and hold Power off, then tap Safe mode.
Use the device for a short period and check whether it still becomes hot.
## Step 6: Stop Using a Device That Is Too Hot
If the device shows a temperature warning and shuts down repeatedly, stop charging it and contact Samsung Support.

payloads.query: My Galaxy Buds will not pair with my phone any more, they just show as unavailable.

siis_response.title: Bluetooth device will not pair with a Samsung phone
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Mobile Accessories Bluetooth device will not pair with a Samsung phone: # Resolving Bluetooth Pairing Failures
A device that previously paired and now will not usually needs its stored pairing removing.
## Step 1: Remove the Stored Pairing
Open Settings and tap Connections.
Tap Bluetooth, then tap the settings icon next to the device.
Tap Unpair, then put the accessory back into pairing mode and select it again.
## Step 2: Check the Accessory Is Charged
Place both earbuds in the charging case and confirm the case has charge.
An accessory with a flat battery will not appear in the list.
## Step 3: Restart Bluetooth
Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the Quick settings panel.
Turn Bluetooth off, wait a few seconds, then turn it back on.
## Step 4: Clear the Bluetooth Cache
Open Settings and tap Apps.
Tap More options, then Show system apps.
Select Bluetooth, tap Storage, then tap Clear cache.
## Step 5: Reset the Accessory
Place both earbuds in the case, close the lid, and hold the touchpads for ten seconds to reset them.
## Step 6: Reset Network Settings
Open Settings and tap General management.
Tap Reset, then tap Reset network settings, which also clears Bluetooth pairings.

payloads.query: I stopped getting notifications from WhatsApp and only see them when I actually open the app.

siis_response.title: Notifications are delayed or missing for an app
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Notifications are delayed or missing for an app: # Restoring App Notifications
Missing notifications are almost always a battery or notification permission setting rather than a fault.
## Step 1: Confirm Notifications Are Allowed
Open Settings and tap Notifications.
Tap App notifications and confirm the app is turned on.
## Step 2: Stop the Device Sleeping the App
Open Settings and tap Battery.
Tap Background usage limits, then tap Deep sleeping apps.
Remove the app from that list if it appears there.
## Step 3: Turn Off Power Saving for the App
Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select the app, tap Battery, then select Unrestricted.
## Step 4: Check Do Not Disturb
Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the Quick settings panel.
Confirm Do not disturb is turned off.
## Step 5: Clear the App Cache
Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select the app, tap Storage, then tap Clear cache.

payloads.query: My phone charges really slowly now, it takes most of the night to fill up.

siis_response.title: Device charges slowly on a Samsung phone or tablet
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet Device charges slowly on a Samsung phone or tablet: # Improving Charging Speed
Slow charging is usually the cable, the adapter, or a setting rather than the battery.
## Step 1: Inspect the Cable and Port
Check the cable for damage and the charging port for lint or debris.
Shine a light into the port and clear it gently with a dry brush.
## Step 2: Use a Fast Charging Adapter
Charge with the adapter supplied with the device.
Charging from a computer USB port is significantly slower.
## Step 3: Turn On Fast Charging
Open Settings and tap Battery.
Tap More battery settings and turn on Fast charging.
## Step 4: Avoid Using the Device While Charging
Put the device down and turn off the screen while it charges.
Using navigation or games while charging can cancel out the incoming power.
## Step 5: Charge in a Cooler Place
A hot device charges more slowly to protect the battery.
Move it out of direct sunlight and remove the case.
## Step 6: Have the Battery Checked
If charging is still slow with the original adapter, contact Samsung Support to arrange a battery health check.
